topics.title: Chemistry Nobel honors mirrored molecules
topics.summary: Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai won the 2026 Nobel Prize in chemistry for discoveries about mirror-image molecules that helped shape modern medicines and molecular research.
topics.discussionPrompt: If two molecules can be mirror twins with totally different effects, who wants the chemistry demo and who starts comparing it to identical cousins?

topics.title: IMF warns on debt and AI
topics.summary: IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva urged governments to curb record debt while also preparing clearer rules for artificial intelligence and high energy costs.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a global money boss says debt, AI, and energy are all tangled together, who asks for the spreadsheet and who asks for coffee first?

topics.title: Markets pull back from records
topics.summary: U.S. stocks retreated from record highs as global markets fell, with investors watching bond yields, French budget worries, oil prices and the broader economic outlook.
topics.discussionPrompt: When markets dip after hitting records, who calls it a healthy breather and who immediately checks every account password they own?

topics.title: Ukraine faces major overnight attack
topics.summary: Russia launched a large missile and drone attack across Kyiv and other Ukrainian regions, while Ukrainian officials continued seeking more air-defense support.
topics.discussionPrompt: When air defense becomes the whole conversation, who focuses on the engineering challenge and who focuses on how people keep daily life going?

topics.title: El Nino questions go global
topics.summary: A powerful El Nino is being linked to extreme weather around the world, with climate journalists fielding public questions about risks, records and preparation.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the weather pattern gets a blockbuster nickname, who wants the science behind it and who starts rating which cities need the biggest umbrella?

topics.title: Researchers question techno-optimism
topics.summary: A new climate-focused study reported that scientists who put stronger faith in technology may be less likely to support immediate climate action.
topics.discussionPrompt: When someone says future tech will fix everything, who nods along and who asks what we are doing before the future arrives?

topics.title: BBC tracks tense Israel anniversary
topics.summary: Israel marked three years since the October 7 attacks, with memorials and difficult conversations about rebuilding communities near the Gaza border.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a community debates whether to rebuild after trauma, who thinks about home first and who thinks about whether home can feel the same again?

topics.title: France reviews protest policing tool
topics.summary: France halted the use of stun grenades after a student protest injury, following complaints that police tactics toward teenagers had become disproportionate.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a crowd-control tool gets paused, who talks public safety first and who asks how protests stay loud without turning dangerous?

topics.title: Oil tanker burns near Sochi
topics.summary: A naval drone hit an oil tanker off Russia's Black Sea coast near Sochi, sparking a large fire while officials said the crew was rescued.
topics.discussionPrompt: When conflict reaches shipping lanes, who starts mapping trade routes and who wonders how crews train for a crisis at sea?

topics.title: Smart glasses scrutiny keeps growing
topics.summary: Privacy concerns around camera-enabled smart glasses continued to build, with regulators and governments weighing restrictions, safety checks and public-space rules.
topics.discussionPrompt: If glasses can quietly record, who loves the gadget future and who wants every pair to blink like a lighthouse when filming?
